title: Directional End-Zone Possession
objective: Develop players’ ability to maintain possession while moving the football purposefully towards a defined scoring end.
setup:
Create a rectangular playing area with a five-metre scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two even teams.
One team attacks one end while the opposition attacks the opposite end.
Begin with one football and position players throughout the area.
Tackling is replaced by touch pressure for younger or less experienced groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts play by releasing the football to one team near the centre.
The team in possession attempts to move the football into its attacking scoring zone.
Players may kick or handball and may move freely throughout the area.
A point is scored when a player receives a legal disposal inside the attacking scoring zone.
The receiving player must enter the zone after the disposal has been released.
Following a score, the opposition restarts from its defensive scoring line.
A turnover occurs after an interception, dropped mark, out-of-bounds disposal or rule infringement.
Play continues for two- to three-minute rounds before teams change attacking directions.
coachingPoints: Encourage players to look forward before using a sideways or backward option.
Create width around the ball carrier to open central passing lanes.
Lead into space rather than standing beside a defender.
Support behind and beside the football so possession can be retained.
Use the appropriate disposal for the available distance and pressure.
Defenders should protect the scoring zone while applying pressure to the football.
Players must transition immediately when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain awareness of the attacking direction.
Whether the team creates usable width around the football.
Whether players lead forward rather than crowding the ball carrier.
Whether the ball carrier scans before disposing.
Whether defenders recover towards the scoring zone after losing pressure.
Whether both teams react quickly after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd around the football.
commonErrors.correction: Stop play and reposition players across the width of the area.

commonErrors.error: The ball is moved sideways without gaining ground.
commonErrors.correction: Reward forward disposals and forward receiving positions.

commonErrors.error: Players wait inside the scoring zone.
commonErrors.correction: Require receivers to enter the zone after the disposal is released.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase the football and leave the scoring zone open.
commonErrors.correction: Coach the deepest defender to protect space behind the press.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate support movement after every disposal.

progressions: Reduce the playing area to increase pressure.
Introduce full legal tackling for appropriate groups.
Require a minimum number of disposals before scoring.
Award two points for a scoring-zone mark from a kick.
Add a ten-second possession limit.
Require the attacking team to use both sides of the area before scoring.
regressions: Add a neutral player who always supports the team in possession.
Allow defenders to apply delayed pressure after each restart.
Permit a stationary receiver inside the scoring zone for Under 8 players.
successIndicators: Move the football towards the correct attacking end.
Create forward and lateral options for the ball carrier.
Enter the scoring zone with timing rather than waiting inside it.
Recover their defensive position immediately after turnovers.
matchApplication: The game introduces the basic tactical requirement of Australian football: win possession, spread from the contest, move the football towards goal and defend space when possession is lost.

title: Blind-Side Support Game
primarySkill: Supporting from the defender’s blind side
objective: Develop players’ ability to create support options from positions outside a defender’s immediate vision.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Place several movement markers five to eight metres outside the central corridor.
Divide players into two teams.
Bonus points are awarded when a receiver arrives from behind or outside a defender’s visual field.
The movement must remain legal and avoid blocking.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with one team in possession.
Off-ball attackers position outside the immediate sightline of their defender.
As the ball carrier scans, the attacker moves into a visible receiving lane.
A completed disposal to a blind-side support runner earns one movement bonus.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score following a blind-side support bonus earns two points.
Defenders must scan both the football and their opponent.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Players rotate support and high-forward roles.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Begin outside the defender’s direct vision.
Move late enough to preserve surprise but early enough to be seen by the ball carrier.
Enter a clear disposal lane.
Communicate without revealing movement too early.
The ball carrier should scan beyond the immediate defender.
Avoid running into a teammate’s space.
Defenders must use shoulder checks.
Maintain legal spacing and avoid screening opponents.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers begin from genuine blind-side positions.
Whether movement is timed effectively.
Whether the ball carrier sees the late option.
Whether runners enter clear lanes.
Whether defenders shoulder-check.
Whether movement remains legal and safe.
Whether support is still provided behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The attacker moves too early and becomes visible.
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the defender’s attention shifts to the football.

commonErrors.error: The runner remains hidden from the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Move into a clear sightline before calling.

commonErrors.error: The runner enters occupied space.
commonErrors.correction: Scan teammate positions before moving.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier focuses only on the nearest option.
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the first defender.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch only the football.
commonErrors.correction: Use repeated shoulder checks to locate opponents.

progressions: Reduce field width.
Apply a three-second disposal limit.
Introduce full legal contact.
Award bonus points for blind-side movement into the scoring zone.
Remove movement markers.
Require defenders to nominate responsibility after each passage.
regressions: Allow the coach to cue movement.
Slow the speed of play during the first round.
matchApplication: The game develops deceptive off-ball movement used to create uncontested receivers, support ball carriers and exploit defenders who become focused on the football.

title: Chaos Ball Recovery Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to react to unpredictable football movement, secure possession and organise the next phase under pressure.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Place the coach outside the middle of the playing area with several footballs.
The coach may roll, bounce, handball, kick or deflect the football into different spaces.
Players begin spread throughout the field.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases an unpredictable football into the playing area.
Both teams react and compete for possession.
The team that secures the football attacks its nominated scoring end.
The opposition immediately organises pressure and defensive protection.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within five disposals of the coach’s release earns two points.
If the football leaves the area, the coach immediately releases a new football.
The coach may release a second football only after the first passage has clearly ended.
Players reset their spread after each score.
Rotate attacking directions between rounds.
coachingPoints: React to the football’s movement rather than guessing.
Slow the final steps when approaching an awkward bounce.
Keep the body behind the football.
Communicate who is attacking the ball and who is supporting.
Take clean possession when possible.
Use the first disposal to escape immediate pressure.
Defenders should react to both the football and dangerous space.
Spread quickly once possession is controlled.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players adjust their approach to the football’s movement.
Whether teammates communicate contest and support roles.
Whether players keep their feet where possible.
Whether possession is secured rather than knocked forward without purpose.
Whether the first disposal exits pressure.
Whether defenders protect the scoring side.
Whether players react immediately to a new release.

commonErrors.error: Players charge at an unpredictable bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and remain balanced.

commonErrors.error: Several teammates attack the same football.
commonErrors.correction: Call one player in and organise support around them.

commonErrors.error: Players tap the football without a clear purpose.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession unless a controlled knock creates advantage.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal remains inside congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the open release side before collecting.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after the football leaves the area.
commonErrors.correction: Expect an immediate new football and reset quickly.

progressions: Increase the unpredictability of releases.
Reduce the playing area.
Introduce full legal tackling.
Release the football near the boundary.
Award defensive points for trapping the ball winner.
Start selected passages with one team outnumbered.
Add wet-weather footballs where conditions and safety permit.
regressions: Begin with one player nominated to attack the football.
successIndicators: Spread or recover defensively after the contest.
matchApplication: The game recreates the unpredictable bounces, spills, deflections and loose footballs that occur throughout Australian football and require immediate technical and tactical adjustment.

title: Smother-to-Score Game
primarySkill: Applying and responding to smother pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to apply safe smother pressure, recover the deflected football and transition immediately into attack.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark two narrow pressure lanes through the middle.
Divide players into two teams.
Players may kick or handball normally.
Defenders are rewarded for legal smother attempts that contact the football.
Safety instructions must be reinforced before play begins.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession.
Defenders close space and attempt legal smothers when a kick is predictable.
A successful smother earns one defensive point.
The football remains live after the smother.
The team that recovers the loose football attacks its nominated end.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within four disposals of a smother earns two points.
Unsafe diving or contact with the kicker results in an immediate stoppage and turnover.
Teams play ninety-second high-intensity rounds.
Rotate defensive match-ups and starting possession.
coachingPoints: Close quickly and shorten the final steps.
Smother with hands and arms extended towards the football.
Do not make contact with the kicker’s legs.
Read the kicker’s preparation and disposal line.
Recover immediately after the smother attempt.
Teammates should anticipate the likely deflection.
Ball carriers should use composure, footwork and disposal choice to avoid predictable kicks.
Maintain safe body position throughout.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders approach under control.
Whether smother technique is legal and safe.
Whether players anticipate the deflection.
Whether the smothering player recovers quickly.
Whether ball carriers recognise pressure before kicking.
Whether players use handball or evasion when the kick is blocked.
Whether turnovers become organised attack.

commonErrors.error: Defenders dive recklessly at the kicker.
commonErrors.correction: Stay upright or controlled and target the football only.

commonErrors.error: The smothering player stops after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Recover immediately and locate the deflection.

commonErrors.error: Teammates react late to the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: Anticipate the likely spill before the smother occurs.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers telegraph the kick.
commonErrors.correction: Use scanning, footwork and shorter preparation.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt smothers from unsafe angles.
commonErrors.correction: Approach from the front or controlled side angle.

progressions: Reduce the playing area.
Apply a three-second disposal limit.
Award an extra point for recovering the smothered football.
Introduce full legal tackling after the deflection.
Start selected possessions inside a pressure lane.
Require one kick before scoring.
Add scoreboard consequences for smother turnovers.
regressions: Practise controlled shadow smothers before live play.
Allow protected possession after a mark.
Count near-smothers that clearly alter the kick.
matchApplication: The game develops smother pressure and recovery during congested phases, forward-half defence and close-range disposal situations.

title: Small-Sided Pressure Phase Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to apply the complete pressure-and-contest principles developed across SG-041 to SG-059 during realistic and demanding small-sided play.
setup:
Create a directional field with a central pressure box.
Mark one boundary trap zone and two outside release gates.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare assessment categories covering contested possession, release support, pressing, intercept positioning, repeat pressure, aerial organisation, pressure transfer and decision making under fatigue.
Conduct four progressive assessment rounds.
Adjust contact and workload to suit age, experience and player condition.
howTheDrillWorks:
Round one begins each possession with a contested football inside the central pressure box.
Round two begins with a high aerial ball and rewards organised marking, spoiling and ground-level recovery.
Round three uses continuous play with defensive points for intercepts, smothers, trap-zone turnovers and connected pressure transfers.
Round four removes all starting constraints and introduces a live score-and-time scenario.
A scoring-zone receive earns one attacking point.
A score completed within five disposals of a contest or turnover win earns two points.
A clean intercept, legal smother recovery or trap-zone turnover earns one defensive point.
Three connected pressure transfers earn one defensive point.
Teams receive one minute between rounds to review one pressure or contest priority.
The coach records individual and team behaviours without unnecessary stoppages.
The final round is played without coach instruction.
The assessment ends if fatigue causes unsafe contact or unacceptable skill deterioration.
coachingPoints: Establish body position before contesting.
Protect possession when outnumbered.
Maintain inside and outside balance.
Spread rapidly after a contest win.
Apply coordinated pressure rather than individual chasing.
Protect the corridor and dangerous scoring space.
Transfer defensive responsibility early.
Recover after tackles, smothers and corrals.
Organise aerial and ground-level roles.
Preserve decision quality under fatigue.
Transition immediately after turnovers.
Maintain legal and controlled contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players establish effective contest position.
Whether outnumbered players protect and delay.
Whether outside support remains available.
Whether teams spread after winning possession.
Whether defensive pressure remains connected.
Whether corridor and scoring-zone protection are maintained.
Whether pressure responsibility transfers smoothly.
Whether smothers and tackles are safe.
Whether aerial and ground-level players organise correctly.
Whether skill and decision quality remain under fatigue.
Whether players transition immediately.
Whether teams adjust independently between rounds.

commonErrors.error: Too many players collapse into the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Retain outside support and defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: Pressure becomes individual and disconnected.
commonErrors.correction: Assign pressure, support and protection roles.

commonErrors.error: Players chase turnovers and leave dangerous space.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the scoring side before attacking the football.

commonErrors.error: Defensive transfers occur too late.
commonErrors.correction: Move and communicate while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner rushes the release disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the first effective option.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes unsafe contact or poor technique.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce load, shorten rounds or stop the assessment.

progressions: Introduce full match-like contact for appropriate groups.
Reduce field dimensions.
Remove visual zones and gates.
Add changing numerical advantage.
Use hidden tactical objectives.
Apply a three-second disposal limit.
Assess players by positional role.
Add late-game scoreboard and time pressure.
regressions: Reduce round length and total workload.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the pressure, contest, defensive trap, aerial recovery and fatigue-management behaviours required during demanding phases of Australian football.
relatedDrills: SG-047 – Repeat Pressure and Recover Game
SG-050 – Pressure and Contest Fundamentals Assessment

title: Handball Release to Kick Connection
primarySkill: Linking handball release with kick-mark possession
objective: Develop players’ ability to use handball to escape immediate pressure before connecting with a controlled forward kick.
setup:
Create a directional field with a ten-metre central release zone.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
When possession is won inside the release zone, the first disposal must be a handball.
The next effective disposal must be a kick.
Outside the release zone, normal disposal choice applies.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts each possession with a loose football or short disposal inside the central release zone.
The team winning possession uses handball to release the football from pressure.
The next receiver attempts to complete a forward kick to a moving teammate.
Once the kick is completed, play continues normally.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed through a clean handball-release-to-mark sequence earns two points.
A turnover reverses the attacking direction.
Defenders may pressure the release and close the kick receiver.
Players rotate through inside, release and forward-link roles.
Play continues for three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Protect the football before the release handball.
Outside runners must move before the contest is won.
Handball into the receiver’s path.
The release player should scan before receiving.
Balance quickly before kicking.
Forward targets must lead into visible space.
Do not force the kick if the receiver remains under pressure.
Defenders should pressure the release while protecting the next kick option.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial handball exits pressure.
Whether outside support moves early.
Whether the release player scans before receiving.
Whether the kick is balanced and purposeful.
Whether forward targets time their leads.
Whether defenders connect pressure across both disposals.
Whether teams retain structure after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: The release handball goes to a stationary player.
commonErrors.correction: The outside receiver must move before possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: The kicker disposes while off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Take enough steps to stabilise before kicking.

commonErrors.error: The next lead starts too early.
commonErrors.correction: Lead as the release handball reaches the outside player.

commonErrors.error: Players force the kick into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until a clear target appears.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after pressure on the first possession.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer pressure immediately to the release player.

progressions: Reduce the release-zone size.
Apply a two-second limit to the release player.
Introduce full legal tackling.
Require the kick to travel at least 15 metres.
Award defensive points for intercepting the first kick.
Begin with uneven numbers inside the release zone.
Remove the compulsory disposal sequence during the final round.
regressions: Protect the release receiver for two seconds.
Allow either the first or second disposal to be a handball.
Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
matchApplication: The game develops the common match sequence of winning possession inside congestion, releasing by handball and then connecting through a controlled kick.

title: Team Ball Movement Phase Final Assessment
Advantage Call Continuation Game
primarySkill: Continuing play after an infringement or broken contest
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise when an advantage exists and continue play effectively rather than stopping after an infringement or contested incident.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
The coach acts as umpire.
During play, the coach may call an infringement and then signal:
advantage;
free kick;
play on.
Players must react to the complete call rather than the whistle alone.
Controlled contact rules must be clearly established.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession.
Play continues under normal small-sided-game rules.
The coach calls selected infringements or simulated free kicks.
When advantage is called, the team with possession continues without stopping.
If no advantage exists, the coach awards the free kick.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score completed within five seconds of an advantage call earns two points.
The opposition earns one defensive point if it recovers and stops the advantage before a scoring attempt.
Players who stop on the whistle despite an advantage call remain out of the passage until they recover their position.
Play continues for two-minute rounds.
Teams review their reactions between rounds.
coachingPoints: Listen to the complete umpire call.
Continue moving until play is clearly stopped.
The ball carrier should assess whether the advantage is genuine.
Teammates must support immediately after the call.
Defenders must recover even when they expect a free kick.
Avoid taking an advantage into greater pressure.
Maintain legal contact and avoid arguing with decisions.
Communicate whether the team should continue or take the free kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players stop at the whistle.
Whether the ball carrier recognises genuine advantage.
Whether teammates continue supporting.
Whether defenders recover immediately.
Whether players understand free-kick and play-on signals.
Whether advantage decisions improve or worsen possession.
Whether emotional reactions distract players from the next action.

commonErrors.error: Players stop immediately at the whistle.
commonErrors.correction: Continue until the umpire clearly stops play.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier takes advantage into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Accept advantage only when it creates a better position.

commonErrors.error: Teammates assume the free kick will be taken.
commonErrors.correction: Continue moving until the decision is clear.

commonErrors.error: Defenders appeal instead of recovering.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the next action before responding to the decision.

commonErrors.error: Players argue with the call.
commonErrors.correction: Refocus immediately on possession and positioning.

progressions: Use less predictable advantage calls.
Apply full legal contact for suitable groups.
Introduce scoreboard and time pressure.
Allow a player to choose whether to take the advantage.
Add deliberate out-of-bounds and holding-the-football scenarios.
Remove verbal explanation and use umpire signals only.
Rotate players through an umpiring role.
regressions: Announce the likely call before the passage.
Use only advantage and free-kick calls.
Allow the coach to repeat the call.
matchApplication: The game develops realistic response to advantage, play-on and free-kick situations where players must continue competing until the umpire has clearly stopped play.

title: Mismatch Identification Game
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify a favourable attacking match-up and use team structure to create an effective scoring opportunity.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Before each round, the coach discreetly identifies one favourable attacking match-up using a wristband, bib marker or player number.
The attacking team is told which teammate has the potential mismatch.
The defence is not told directly but may identify it through play.
Normal Australian football rules apply.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in the attacking team’s defensive or midfield half.
The attacking team attempts to identify the location of the favourable match-up.
Teammates create space around the target player.
The ball may be moved elsewhere first to improve the eventual entry.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score created through the nominated mismatch earns two points.
A score through another clearly superior option still earns one point.
Defenders may provide help, switch opponents or protect space.
A turnover immediately reverses attacking direction.
The coach changes the nominated mismatch between rounds.
Players review whether the mismatch was used appropriately or forced.
coachingPoints: Identify the match-up before entering the attacking half.
Create space around the favourable target.
Do not reveal the intended target too early.
Use switches and ball movement to isolate the match-up.
Kick to the target’s advantage.
Do not force the mismatch if defensive help removes the advantage.
Defenders should communicate support and opponent transfers.
Maintain turnover protection behind the attack.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the nominated target.
Whether teammates create isolation space.
Whether the football is moved to improve the entry angle.
Whether the mismatch remains favourable at the moment of disposal.
Whether players ignore superior alternative options.
Whether defenders identify and support the vulnerable match-up.
Whether the attacking team protects against turnover.

commonErrors.error: Players kick immediately to the mismatch from a poor angle.
commonErrors.correction: Move the football until the entry improves.

commonErrors.error: Teammates crowd the target player.
commonErrors.correction: Clear the surrounding space.

commonErrors.error: The target reveals the lead too early.
commonErrors.correction: Delay movement until the ball carrier is ready.

commonErrors.error: Players force the matchup after defensive support arrives.
commonErrors.correction: Use the spare player created by the defensive help.

commonErrors.error: Defenders fail to communicate support.
commonErrors.correction: Call the mismatch and organise help early.

progressions: Change the mismatch during live play.
Introduce full legal contact.
Give both teams a nominated mismatch.
Apply a ten-second scoring limit.
Allow defenders to switch freely.
Remove visual match-up markers.
Use score-and-time scenarios requiring deliberate mismatch selection.
regressions: Clearly identify the target player to both teams.
Protect the first possession near the mismatch.
Begin play in the attacking half.
successIndicators: Improve the entry angle before attacking.
Use the spare player created by defensive help.
matchApplication: The game develops the ability to recognise and exploit height, speed, strength or positioning advantages while responding to defensive support and opponent changes.

title: Clearance to End-Zone Conversion
primarySkill: Converting stoppage possession into a scoring opportunity
objective: Develop players’ ability to turn a stoppage win into an organised scoring opportunity before the opposition can restore defensive structure.
setup:
Mark three possible stoppage-start circles through the middle third.
Create a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
Position inside midfielders, outside players, forwards and defenders.
Each passage begins with a ball-up, boundary-style release or ground-ball stoppage.
The team winning the clearance has ten seconds to attempt a scoring-zone entry.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach selects one stoppage circle and releases the football.
Players compete for possession.
The winning team attempts to release the football to an outside player or forward-facing midfielder.
The ten-second conversion count begins once possession is clearly controlled.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone within ten seconds earns two points.
The defending team earns one point if it delays the attack beyond ten seconds.
If the defending team wins possession, it counterattacks towards the opposite end.
A score after an opposition stoppage win earns two counterattack points.
Rotate stoppage and outside roles after each passage.
Vary the start location and defensive setup.
Play continues for repeated passages.
coachingPoints: Win the football with a clear release plan.
Outside players must move before possession is secured.
The first receiver should face or move towards the attacking end.
Use handball to escape immediate pressure.
Forward players should create width and separate their leads.
Avoid rushing a low-percentage kick solely because of the countdown.
Defenders should pressure the clearance source and protect central space.
If the fast conversion is unavailable, retain possession rather than concede an easy turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the stoppage win has an intended release.
Whether outside players hold useful width.
Whether the first receiver can face forward.
Whether forward movement begins early.
Whether the countdown creates poor decision making.
Whether defenders delay and protect dangerous space.
Whether teams retain possession when immediate conversion is unavailable.
Whether counterattack begins immediately after a defensive win.

commonErrors.error: The clearance is won without outside support.
commonErrors.correction: Position release players before the stoppage begins.

commonErrors.error: The first receiver faces backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Move into a forward-facing position before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Every forward leads towards the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Separate by width, depth and direction.

commonErrors.error: Players force a scoring entry because of the countdown.
commonErrors.correction: Use the first effective option, not the first possible option.

commonErrors.error: Defenders all attack the stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Retain central and deep protection.

progressions: Reduce the conversion time to eight seconds.
Introduce full legal contact.
Start from boundary and forward-50 stoppages.
Begin selected passages with one team outnumbered.
Award three points for a clearance-to-mark conversion.
Allow the defending team to select its stoppage setup.
Remove the visible stoppage circles.
regressions: Begin with one team guaranteed possession.
Stop after the first disposal for positional review.
successIndicators: Win possession with a release option.
Defend the clearance as a unit.
Retain possession when the fast score is unavailable.
matchApplication: The game develops conversion from centre and around-ground stoppages into forward entries before the opposition can reset behind the football.

title: Come-From-Behind Surge
objective: Develop players’ ability to increase attacking urgency and generate scoring opportunities while trailing late in a match without abandoning team structure.
setup:
Create a directional playing area with a scoring zone at each end.
Divide players into two teams.
One team begins four to twelve points behind.
Set the clock between ninety seconds and three minutes.
The trailing team begins with possession in the middle or defensive half.
New footballs are available for rapid restarts.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score and remaining time.
The trailing team attacks immediately.
Normal scoring values apply.
After any score, the coach quickly restarts play from the centre or a nominated location.
If the leading team wins possession, it may retain the football or counterattack.
The trailing team applies immediate pressure after every turnover.
A scoring-zone mark within ten seconds of possession gain earns one bonus point.
A turnover in the trailing team’s defensive area may result in an opposition bonus score.
The scenario ends when time expires.
Teams review whether urgency improved or damaged decision quality.
Roles reverse for the next scenario.
Starting margin and field position change regularly.
coachingPoints: Increase ball and player speed together.
Attack forward when genuine advantage exists.
Retain width and support despite urgency.
Avoid every player moving ahead of the football.
Use the boundary and stoppages only when they help the situation.
After turnover, the nearest player applies immediate pressure.
Maintain at least one player in defensive protection.
Know how many scores are required.
Leaders must communicate remaining time and scoring priorities.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the trailing team understands the required score.
Whether ball speed increases.
Whether width and support remain.
Whether players force low-percentage entries.
Whether defensive protection remains.
Whether turnover pressure is immediate.
Whether the leading team manages possession intelligently.
Whether communication includes score and time.

commonErrors.error: Players rush the first disposal forward.
commonErrors.correction: Use the fastest effective option, not the fastest possible option.

commonErrors.error: Every player runs ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one or two players in protection.

commonErrors.error: The team becomes narrow.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain outside lanes to open central space.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt low-percentage scoring options.
commonErrors.correction: Create a better angle if time permits.

commonErrors.error: The leading team becomes completely passive.
commonErrors.correction: Continue presenting active possession options.

progressions: Reduce the remaining time.
Increase the required margin.
Introduce full legal contact.
Start the trailing team deep in defence.
Hide the exact time remaining.
Require multiple different scorers.
Add deliberate rushed-behind and stoppage scenarios.
matchApplication: The game prepares teams to attack aggressively and intelligently when trailing late in a quarter or match.

title: Interchange Imbalance Game
primarySkill: Adjusting structure during temporary player imbalance
objective: Develop players’ ability to adapt team structure when rotations, injury, discipline or delayed interchange create temporary uneven numbers.
setup:
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark an interchange gate on each side.
Divide players into two teams with substitutes.
The coach may direct a player to leave or delay a replacement.
Teams may temporarily play one or two players short.
Players are not told exactly how long the imbalance will last.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with equal numbers.
The coach signals a player to leave through an interchange gate.
The replacement enters after a delayed signal.
The outnumbered team must reorganise and protect dangerous space.
The team with extra numbers attempts to identify and use the spare player.
A scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A score while using a temporary numerical advantage earns two points.
A defensive stop while outnumbered earns one point.
Once numbers equalise, both teams must restore normal structure.
The coach varies which line loses or gains a player.
Players rotate through interchange roles.
Play continues in three-minute rounds.
coachingPoints: Count numbers immediately after every interchange signal.
The outnumbered team should protect central and deep space.
Delay the attack rather than chasing every opponent.
The team with extra numbers should create width.
Use the spare player before the opposition reorganises.
Communicate which role must be covered.
Once numbers equalise, reset normal structure.
Manage player workload and avoid unsafe repeated overloads.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the imbalance.
Whether the outnumbered team reorganises.
Whether the extra player creates genuine advantage.
Whether players communicate role changes.
Whether central and deep protection remain.
Whether normal structure returns.
Whether fatigue affects the players covering extra space.
Whether teams remain composed during unexpected changes.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to notice that a teammate has left.
commonErrors.correction: Use immediate number and role calls.

commonErrors.error: The outnumbered team continues pressing aggressively.
commonErrors.correction: Delay and protect dangerous space.

commonErrors.error: The spare player moves into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Create width or depth away from defenders.

commonErrors.error: Players keep covering temporary roles after numbers equalise.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish normal match-ups and structure.

commonErrors.error: Workload becomes excessive for the outnumbered team.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the imbalance and rotate roles.

progressions: Remove verbal coach signals and use visual cues.
Create two-player imbalances.
Introduce full legal contact.
Change player numbers during a stoppage.
Add score-and-time scenarios.
Delay the replacement for longer.
Require the outnumbered team to attack after winning possession.
regressions: Announce the number change before it occurs.
Stop briefly for teams to reorganise.
Reduce field size carefully without increasing unsafe congestion.
successIndicators: Use the spare player when advantaged.
matchApplication: The game replicates temporary player imbalances caused by interchange delays, injury, discipline, rotations or players caught away from position.

title: Wet-Weather Territory Game
primarySkill: Territory and possession decisions in wet conditions
objective: Develop players’ ability to adjust technique, risk and field-position decisions when wet conditions reduce marking and disposal reliability.
setup:
Conduct only when the surface is safe and free from standing water, holes or hazardous slipping areas.
Create a directional field with a scoring zone at each end.
Mark two territory lines across the field.
Divide players into two teams.
Use damp footballs or naturally wet conditions.
Reduce contact where footing is uncertain.
A team gains one territory point when it moves the football across a territory line under control.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in possession.
Players attempt to gain territory towards their scoring end.
A controlled possession across a territory line earns one point.
A scoring-zone receive earns two points.
A kick that safely gains territory and reaches the boundary without an opposition touch earns one territory point.
A clean ground-ball win after a spill earns one contest bonus.
A turnover immediately reverses attacking direction.
Players may use shorter disposals when conditions require.
The coach stops play if footing, contact or visibility becomes unsafe.
Teams play two- to three-minute rounds.
Footballs and hands may be dried between rounds.
Modify workload for cold or older players.
coachingPoints: Keep the body behind the football.
Slow the final steps approaching ground balls.
Use two hands when possible.
Lower kicks and shorter disposals may be more reliable.
Do not attempt dangerous sliding or diving.
Accept territory when clean possession is unlikely.
Use the boundary strategically.
Support close enough for shorter disposals.
Defenders should remain balanced and avoid overcommitting on slippery ground.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players adjust their approach speed.
Whether players keep their body behind the football.
Whether disposal length matches the conditions.
Whether teams accept territory when appropriate.
Whether support distances shorten.
Whether boundary use is purposeful.
Whether players attempt unsafe movements.
Whether footwear and surface conditions remain suitable.

commonErrors.error: Players charge at slippery ground balls.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the final steps and lower the body.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt one-handed pickups unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Use two hands and secure the football.

commonErrors.error: Long, high kicks are repeatedly turned over.
commonErrors.correction: Use lower, shorter or territorial options.

commonErrors.error: Players slide into contests.
commonErrors.correction: Stay on the feet and prioritise safety.

commonErrors.error: Teammates remain too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten support distances.

commonErrors.error: Defenders overrun opponents on wet ground.
commonErrors.correction: Close under control with shorter steps.

progressions: Reduce the field width.
Add controlled tackling only when footing is safe.
Require a minimum territorial gain before scoring.
Begin passages with unpredictable wet ground balls.
Add boundary restarts.
Use scoreboard scenarios.
Award defensive points for trapping possession in wet conditions.
regressions: Use damp rather than fully wet footballs.
Remove scoring and focus only on territory and technique.
matchApplication: The game prepares players for wet-weather football where possession is less reliable and territory, body position, short support and safety become increasingly important.

title: Coachless Match Simulation
objective: Develop players’ ability to organise, lead and adjust a match simulation without active coach instruction.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams begin from their selected starting structures.
Play proceeds as a continuous match simulation.
Normal scoring values apply.
Teams manage restarts, stoppages, interchanges and positional changes.
At the end of each five-minute period, teams receive a ninety-second player-led break.
Players identify one problem and one adjustment.
The next period begins with the adjustment applied.
The coach records behaviour but does not direct tactics.
The scoreboard creates changing match priorities.
Captains may call one brief on-field huddle per period.
The final period is played without a formal break.
Players conduct the first post-game review before the coach contributes.
coachingPoints: Leaders should organise without controlling every decision.
Teams must establish clear communication channels.
Tactical adjustments should address observable problems.
Players should manage score, time and territory.
Interchanges must not disrupt team structure.
Stoppage and restart roles must remain clear.
Players should support teammates who change roles.
The coach should intervene only for safety or serious rule issues.
Post-game feedback should begin with player observation.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether teams establish clear structures.
Whether leadership is shared.
Whether communication reaches all lines.
Whether players manage stoppages and interchanges.
Whether scoreboard strategy changes.
Whether tactical adjustments address genuine problems.
Whether role changes are understood.
Whether players remain disciplined without coach direction.
Whether post-game analysis is accurate.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for coach instruction.
commonErrors.correction: Direct tactical questions back to team leaders.

commonErrors.error: One captain controls every decision.
commonErrors.correction: Share responsibility across line leaders.

commonErrors.error: Break discussions include too many changes.
commonErrors.correction: Select one priority adjustment.

commonErrors.error: Interchanges leave positions uncovered.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the replacement role before leaving.

commonErrors.error: Teams ignore the scoreboard.
commonErrors.correction: Assign a player to communicate score and time.

commonErrors.error: Reviews focus only on disposal mistakes.
commonErrors.correction: Include structure, transition, pressure and decision making.

progressions: Remove formal player-led breaks.
Give teams hidden tactical objectives.
Introduce full match-like contact.
Use uneven player numbers.
Add unpredictable umpire events.
Hide the exact remaining time.
Require players to rotate leadership roles.
Record the game for later player-led review.
regressions: Allow one coach question during breaks.
Reduce the playing area and player numbers.
Predetermine one tactical priority per team.
matchApplication: The game prepares players to solve problems during matches when coaches cannot direct every contest, possession or positional adjustment.

title: Small-Sided Games Chapter Final Assessment
objective: Assess players’ ability to independently apply the technical, tactical, physical and behavioural principles developed throughout the complete Small-Sided Games chapter.
groundSize:
Junior or foundation groups: 35–50 metres long and 25–35 metres wide
Advanced groups: 65–85 metres long and 42–52 metres wide
howTheDrillWorks:
Phase one begins as unrestricted directional small-sided play.
Phase two introduces a contested restart and rewards effective clearance conversion.
Phase three introduces a hidden defensive press or temporary numerical imbalance.
Phase four uses a scoreboard and time scenario.
Phase five becomes a coachless match simulation.
A normal scoring-zone receive earns one point.
A moving mark inside the scoring zone earns two points.
A score created through a recognised tactical advantage earns one additional point.
A defensive intercept, tackle-generated turnover or coordinated pressure sequence earns one defensive point.
Teams receive brief player-led reviews between the first four phases.
The coach records individual and team behaviours without unnecessarily stopping play.
The final phase is played without tactical coach instruction.
Players conduct the first post-assessment review.
The coach records chapter-level strengths, priority improvements and suitable future progressions.
coachingPoints: Maintain clear attacking direction.
Create width, depth and multiple support angles.
Move immediately after disposal.
Use scoring space with correct timing.
React instantly when possession changes.
Protect and release contested possession.
Apply coordinated defensive pressure.
Protect dangerous central space.
Recognise and use numerical advantage.
Switch, reverse or reset when the forward path is closed.
Connect defensive, midfield and attacking lines.
Select scoring options according to value and risk.
Adjust tempo to the scoreboard.
Communicate changing roles and tactical information.
Share leadership.
Preserve technique and decision quality under fatigue.
Apply principles according to the game rather than forcing rehearsed patterns.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain effective spacing.
Whether support options appear before pressure arrives.
Whether movement continues after disposal.
Whether scoring-zone entries are timed.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.
Whether contested possession is protected and released.
Whether defensive pressure is connected.
Whether dangerous central space is protected.
Whether teams recognise changing numbers.
Whether ball movement adapts to the defensive structure.
Whether forward entries create genuine advantage.
Whether rear-side protection remains.
Whether score and time influence decisions.
Whether communication reaches all field lines.
Whether leadership is shared.
Whether players adjust without constant coach direction.
Whether skill quality remains under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd the football and lose field width.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish lanes, depth and outside support.

commonErrors.error: Movement stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue into support, overlap or replacement roles.

commonErrors.error: Teams force forward play into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Switch, reset or reconnect before re-entry.

commonErrors.error: Too many players commit to contests.
commonErrors.correction: Retain outside support and defensive protection.

commonErrors.error: Defensive pressure becomes individual.
commonErrors.correction: Assign pressure, support and protection roles.

commonErrors.error: Players chase intercepts and abandon dangerous space.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the scoring side before attacking the football.

commonErrors.error: Teams ignore the scoreboard scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the score, time and tactical priority.

commonErrors.error: Leadership is limited to one player.
commonErrors.correction: Share responsibility across lines and roles.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes poor technique or unsafe contact.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce load, shorten phases or stop the assessment.

progressions: Introduce full match-like contact for appropriate groups.
Remove all visual lane, gate and zone markers.
Change several constraints simultaneously.
Use hidden tactical objectives for both teams.
Introduce unpredictable umpire events.
Rotate player numbers and positions.
Hide the exact remaining time.
Assess players by positional role.
Record the game for player-led video analysis.
Allow teams to design the final match scenario.
regressions: Reduce the number of assessment categories.
Change only one constraint per phase.
successIndicators: Win, protect and release contested possession.
Adapt ball movement to opposition structure.
Preserve skill and decision quality under pressure and fatigue.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the complete Small-Sided Games chapter into a realistic Australian football environment requiring technical execution, tactical awareness, physical work rate, communication, leadership and independent problem solving.
